findings.title: Missing prisma import causes runtime ReferenceError
findings.body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but the file never imports prisma. Every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService via getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce tokens never used, stale tokens persist
findings.body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts fetches and stores refreshed tokens in accessTokenParsed but then constructs the jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url, credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.refresh_token. The refresh is wasted and subsequent API calls keep using the expired access token, causing persistent auth failures.

findings.title: Refresh failure check uses statusText instead of ok/status
findings.body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts checks if (response.statusText !== "OK") to detect refresh failure. statusText is implementation-dependent, empty under HTTP/2, and not a reliable success signal. Successful refreshes can throw HttpError while real failures with different statusText pass through to JSON parsing.

findings.title: Zod SafeParse wrapper stored as credential key
findings.body: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) which returns a Zod SafeParse result { success, data/error }, then writes that wrapper object directly to prisma.credential.update data.key. The DB credential becomes { success, data } instead of tokens, so later googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and calendar access breaks.

findings.title: Minimum token schema is malformed and injects fake refresh_token
findings.body: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts builds minimumTokenResponseSchema with computed keys like [z.string().toString()], which evaluates to a literal string such as ZodString, not a catch-all. Extra provider fields are stripped and validation is meaningless. It then mutates the result with refresh_token = "refresh_token" when missing, persisting a bogus refresh token to the database that will corrupt future refreshes.

findings.title: Sync endpoint returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts in sharing mode returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google reads res.data, Hubspot assigns the return directly to HubspotToken and reads .expiresIn, Zoho/Bigin read .data.error. Without parsing JSON, checking response.ok, or normalizing shape, sync mode yields undefined tokens, TypeErrors, and bad DB writes. The POST also sends no Content-Type, no webhook secret, and no error handling.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) where credentialId is credential.id. The helper forwards that value as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. The external service will look up the wrong user, leaking or refreshing tokens for the wrong account.

findings.title: Webhook lacks method check and crashes on bad payload
findings.body: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts accepts any HTTP method and calls schema.parse, JSON.parse, and symmetricDecrypt without try/catch. Invalid bodies, malformed encrypted keys, or wrong encryption key throw uncaught exceptions resulting in 500s instead of 400s, and GET requests can hit DB/decrypt logic unintentionally.
